correctness.rationale: For every integer \(m\ge2\) and real \(a>0\), differentiating the gamma-ratio formula for symmetric Dirichlet moments gives \(\mathbb EH\), \(\mathbb EQ\), and \(\mathbb E[HQ]\); the digamma recurrence leaves \(\operatorname{Cov}(H,Q)=-a(m-1)/[(ma+1)^2(ma+2)]\). Second derivatives and fourth moments give both positive variances. Exact algebraic differences reduce to zero in the standalone checker. The gamma-normalization construction and iid CLT/delta method yield the covariance matrix of the bivariate limit for fixed positive a. The trigamma integral with \(f(t)=1/(1-e^{-t})-1/t\) has \(f'(t)>0\), proving that \(g(x)=x[x\psi_1(x)-1]\) strictly decreases and the limiting correlation strictly decreases. Taylor expansion of trigamma around 1 gives the fixed-m sparse-shape limit and demonstrates the noncommuting iterated limits. Symbolic identities, twelve Monte Carlo cases, and asymptotic numerical checks were separately implemented and executed. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General single-index moment families and integration recipes do not imply cross-moments for differing orders as a stated corollary. The Poisson–Dirichlet alternative entails a distinct scaling of total concentration, so it does not dominate the fixed-a high-dimensional limit. The proof adds a strict integral-monotonicity property, not a simple renaming of previously recorded formulas.

originality.rationale: The claim under review is the complete positive-shape Dirichlet dependence transition, including a strict limiting-correlation monotonicity proof and noncommuting concentration and dimension limits. The special \(a=1\) covariance is already known and excluded from the novelty assertion. Primary full texts on Greenwood (Royen), entropy moments (Wolpert and Wolf), and Tsallis index moments (Cerquetti) provide marginals or single-order moments and do not state or directly dominate the two-index transition. Similar-looking infinite Poisson–Dirichlet laws have a different probability space and parameter asymptotics. Searches found no stronger equivalent; no inference of global novelty follows from a search miss, and a historically plausible inaccessible source remains documented.
residual_risks: Earlier or unindexed joint moments of Shannon and Simpson under symmetric Dirichlet could contain the mixed moment or a stronger parameterized theorem.
Gill and Joanes (1979) primary full PDF was inaccessible; only its title and abstract were reviewed.
The full hierarchy of multi-order Tsallis moment identities, if available elsewhere, could imply the displayed formulas by differentiation.
Prior specializations and infinite-partition analogues must not be represented as newly discovered or independently certified.

value.rationale: The objects are two independently motivated classical measures of diversity/concentration, with applications to random uniform spacings and Greenwood goodness-of-fit statistics. This theorem gives their exact shape-dependent joint association and a strictly monotone, nontrivial continuum of asymptotic correlations, despite both marginal variances shrinking with dimension. Its singular-limit noncommutation identifies a real structural boundary between sparse component shapes and high-dimensional fixed shapes. These are natural dependence questions not fixed by separate marginal moments. The familiar \(a=1\) special case, a routine integration identity in isolation, and an inference claim without data would not meet the value bar; the limiting shape transition and noncommutation are what do.
